To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Wikipedia long tail is large, (2) shrinkage can be applied to the long tail, (3) the training data can be improved by retraining, and (4) Web extraction can be used to supplement Wikipedia extraction.
we have developed techniques for improving information extraction from Wikipedia's long-tail by using a taxonomy, retraining, and extracting from the Web.

(1) a shrinkage-based taxonomy can be learned automatically from Wikipedia's infoboxes; (2) this taxonomy can be used to improve extraction recall from Wikipedia by a factor of up to 8.7; and (3) retraining the extraction system on the improved taxonomy and using Web-based extraction can increase recall further, by a factor of at least 1.7.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of information extraction from Wikipedia.
the question of how to extract information from Wikipedia in a way that is both precise and comprehensive.
the question of how to move beyond the well-populated classes in Wikipedia and extract information from the less populated ones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our methods are effective in extracting information from the long tail of Wikipedia, and that the combination of all our methods is the most effective.
this work is a significant advance over prior work, in the sense of achieving a higher recall while maintaining or increasing the precision.
the proposed techniques are able to increase recall from Wikipedia's tail by an order of magnitude while maintaining or increasing the precision.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, with these techniques, the long tail of Wikipedia's information extraction problem is no longer a problem.
the combination of our three techniques can increase recall of the state-of-the-art system from 0.2% to 1.8%, while maintaining precision.

we are the first to demonstrate that it is feasible to extract information from Wikipedia for the long tail of classes, and that we can achieve a precision of 0.8 or more for a recall of 0.2 or higher.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by combining techniques from the fields of machine learning and information extraction, we can achieve a large gain in recall without sacrificing precision.
Wikipedia's long tail is a rich source of information that can be extracted with high precision and recall, if we can learn from the data.
Wikipedia is not just a source of information but can also be a source of training examples for extracting other types of information. @inproceedings
